<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Walking with Love and
Patience<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">7 March 2018<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">A Vespers reflection based upon Ephesians
2:1-10; Psalm 107; </span><span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">John 3:14-21</span><span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Will you pray with me?  May
the words of my mouth and the meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your
sight O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer. Amen!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">So we have been walking in
the wilderness of Lent for over three weeks now, pondering, thinking,
suffering, and hopefully learning. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">During the recent lock-in,
the youth looked at this scripture from Ephesians.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">I asked what verse stood out.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">There were two raised by the
youth.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">(4) “out of great love with
which God loved us” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">and (5) that “by grace you
have been saved.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Our youth thought some
important words stood out: <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">faith, love and grace. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Apostle Paul reminds also
that “love is patient and love is kind.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">This speaks to our theme
today of walking in the wilderness with God with love and with patience. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">So what Is grace? What is
love?<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">The youth raised some
ideas.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Of grace, they offered the
image of beautiful dancers and talented actors. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">They thought grace was spending
time with loved ones.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Of love, the youth told us
stories about a family inviting someone into their homes. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">They gave examples of how
donations and helping people showed both grace and love. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">They also shared how
patience, appreciation and courtesy are expressions of love. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">(Perhaps someone told them
about Paul’s letter to Corinth.) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Yet, another suggested that
love and grace happen <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">when someone helps another
after a big fall. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">These are great ideas about
how one expresses love and grace.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Even more, we also read “for
by grace you have been saved through faith…; it is the gift of God…” This extends
these ideas. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">We can understand love and
grace as gifts of God. These are simple gifts. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Through faith, we may find those
gifts, right here and right now. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">So if we think about what the
youth were saying about love and patience <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">is that grace is not only a
gift from God but ultimately an expression of God.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Further, if we are love and
patience, are we not an expression of God’s grace?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">But wait Tony, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">What about doing hard work
and following rules to get grace or to Heaven? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">I heard this a lot growing
up. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Hard work and discipline have
benefits.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">While there may be benefit to
observing “lawful traditions,” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Does that prevent you from
doing what is right?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Does that prevent you from welcoming
others to receive this gift?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">So, what are you doing that prevents
you from receiving this gift?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Jesus consistently challenges
the rules and traditions, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">especially when those rules
distort or even prevent God’s Truth. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Let us consider this challenge
in the context of John’s Gospel from this week.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">This Gospel likes to invoke
our senses (e.g. tasting great wine, smelling large odors, touching Jesus,
hearing God speaking, or gaining sight).<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Specifically, the lesson from
John 3:14-21 appeals to our sight;<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">we will “see” the true light
of deeds through God’s truth.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">How do you think your deeds (or
your love) will look in the light? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">How do you let love be in everything
you are?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">What are you doing to prevent
love from being you?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Jesus says Transform and have
faith.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">God’s grace is here, waiting
for us now. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">If you look beyond your
suffering and wilderness, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">you may “see” the light of
God peering out <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">-- shining upon all of our
deeds.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Consider how you make your
deeds a shining example of God’s love for all.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Is that really difficult?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Yet, this letter to Ephesus
reminds us that that is fundamental God – simplicity. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">It is us, like me, who makes
that simplicity complex.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Still, the gift has been here
all the time and waiting.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">That gift is right here and
now <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">-- waiting for us to accept. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">While we are walking with God
in the wilderness,<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">We are reminded that <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">We are not alone in our
brokenness and suffering.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">We don’t let the suffering
stop us from welcoming with open hearts.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">For that, we can share our
gifts given to us.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Be generous and Be kind with
love and patience. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Remind others of how God
expresses love through your hearts and minds. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">With your love and patience
in all seasons – not just a couple times of the year, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Embrace and welcome our
community with warm hugs and helping hands. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">As the youth suggest, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">show your love and grace when
you reach for others that have fallen. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">That grace is right there
when we need it the most and it is a simple gift <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">– no strings attached and no
exceptions.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">That is one way we walk with
God in this wilderness.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Again, we start by letting go
of the suffering -- like a Chinese lantern to the sea.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">We share our compassion and
generosity with a hello and hug.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">We share our genuine love
with patience.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Thus, we become the
expression of God’s grace here and now.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Then, we may find rest in the
wilderness. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">As Children of God, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">we are given that great and
wonderful gift of love and grace. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">because we know that <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">God is good all the time<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">and all the time, God is Good<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="font-size: 14.0pt;">Let us share and be thankful
for God’s gifts of grace and love.</span></div>

 Walking with Love and
Patience 
 
 Tony E Hansen 
 
 7 March 2018 
 

 
 
 A Vespers reflection based upon Ephesians
2:1-10; Psalm 107; John 3:14-21 
 

 
 
 Will you pray with me?  May
the words of my mouth and the meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your
sight O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer. Amen! 
 

 
 
 So we have been walking in
the wilderness of Lent for over three weeks now, pondering, thinking,
suffering, and hopefully learning. 
 
 During the recent lock-in,
the youth looked at this scripture from Ephesians.   
 
 I asked what verse stood out.
 
 
 There were two raised by the
youth.   
 
 (4) “out of great love with
which God loved us” 
 
 and (5) that “by grace you
have been saved.” 
 

 
 
 Our youth thought some
important words stood out: 
 
 faith, love and grace. 
 
 Apostle Paul reminds also
that “love is patient and love is kind.” 
 
 This speaks to our theme
today of walking in the wilderness with God with love and with patience. 
 

 
 
 So what Is grace? What is
love?   
 
 The youth raised some
ideas.   
 
 Of grace, they offered the
image of beautiful dancers and talented actors. 
 
 They thought grace was spending
time with loved ones.   
 
 Of love, the youth told us
stories about a family inviting someone into their homes. 
 
 They gave examples of how
donations and helping people showed both grace and love. 
 
 They also shared how
patience, appreciation and courtesy are expressions of love. 
 
 (Perhaps someone told them
about Paul’s letter to Corinth.) 
 
 Yet, another suggested that
love and grace happen 
 
 when someone helps another
after a big fall. 
 

 
 
 These are great ideas about
how one expresses love and grace. 
 

 
 
 Even more, we also read “for
by grace you have been saved through faith…; it is the gift of God…” This extends
these ideas. 
 

 
 
 We can understand love and
grace as gifts of God. These are simple gifts. 
 
 Through faith, we may find those
gifts, right here and right now. 
 
 So if we think about what the
youth were saying about love and patience 
 
 is that grace is not only a
gift from God but ultimately an expression of God.   
 
 Further, if we are love and
patience, are we not an expression of God’s grace? 
 

 
 
 But wait Tony, 
 
 What about doing hard work
and following rules to get grace or to Heaven? 
 
 I heard this a lot growing
up. 
 
 Hard work and discipline have
benefits. 
 
 While there may be benefit to
observing “lawful traditions,” 
 
 Does that prevent you from
doing what is right? 
 
 Does that prevent you from welcoming
others to receive this gift? 
 

 
 
 So, what are you doing that prevents
you from receiving this gift? 
 

 
 
 Jesus consistently challenges
the rules and traditions, 
 
 especially when those rules
distort or even prevent God’s Truth. 
 

 
 
 Let us consider this challenge
in the context of John’s Gospel from this week. 
 
 This Gospel likes to invoke
our senses (e.g. tasting great wine, smelling large odors, touching Jesus,
hearing God speaking, or gaining sight).  
 
 
 Specifically, the lesson from
John 3:14-21 appeals to our sight; 
 
 we will “see” the true light
of deeds through God’s truth. 
 

 
 
 How do you think your deeds (or
your love) will look in the light? 
 
 How do you let love be in everything
you are? 
 
 What are you doing to prevent
love from being you? 
 

 
 
 Jesus says Transform and have
faith.   
 
 God’s grace is here, waiting
for us now. 
 
 If you look beyond your
suffering and wilderness, 
 
 you may “see” the light of
God peering out 
 
 -- shining upon all of our
deeds.   
 

 
 
 Consider how you make your
deeds a shining example of God’s love for all. 
 
 Is that really difficult? 
 
 Yet, this letter to Ephesus
reminds us that that is fundamental God – simplicity. 
 
 It is us, like me, who makes
that simplicity complex. 
 

 
 
 Still, the gift has been here
all the time and waiting.   
 
 That gift is right here and
now 
 
 -- waiting for us to accept. 
 

 
 
 While we are walking with God
in the wilderness, 
 
 We are reminded that 
 
 We are not alone in our
brokenness and suffering. 
 
 We don’t let the suffering
stop us from welcoming with open hearts. 
 
 For that, we can share our
gifts given to us. 
 
 Be generous and Be kind with
love and patience. 
 
 Remind others of how God
expresses love through your hearts and minds. 
 

 
 
 With your love and patience
in all seasons – not just a couple times of the year, 
 
 Embrace and welcome our
community with warm hugs and helping hands. 
 
 As the youth suggest, 
 
 show your love and grace when
you reach for others that have fallen. 
 
 That grace is right there
when we need it the most and it is a simple gift 
 
 – no strings attached and no
exceptions. 
 

 
 
 That is one way we walk with
God in this wilderness. 
 
 Again, we start by letting go
of the suffering -- like a Chinese lantern to the sea. 
 
 We share our compassion and
generosity with a hello and hug. 
 
 We share our genuine love
with patience. 
 
 Thus, we become the
expression of God’s grace here and now. 
 

 
 
 Then, we may find rest in the
wilderness. 
 

 
 
 As Children of God, 
 
 we are given that great and
wonderful gift of love and grace. 
 
 because we know that 
 

 
 
 God is good all the time 
 
 and all the time, God is Good 
 

 
 
 Let us share and be thankful
for God’s gifts of grace and love.

 Walking with Love and
Patience 
 
 Tony E Hansen 
 
 7 March 2018 
 

 
 
 A Vespers reflection based upon Ephesians
2:1-10; Psalm 107; John 3:14-21 
 

 
 
 Will you pray with me?  May
the words of my mouth and the meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your
sight O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer. Amen! 
 

 
 
 So we have been walking in
the wilderness of Lent for over three weeks now, pondering, thinking,
suffering, and hopefully learning. 
 
 During the recent lock-in,
the youth looked at this scripture from Ephesians.   
 
 I asked what verse stood out.
 
 
 There were two raised by the
youth.

 and (5) that “by grace you
have been saved.”

important words stood out:

<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Walking with Prayerful Humility</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Tony E Hansen</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">14 March 2018</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">A Vespers reflection based upon Psalm
51; Hebrews 5:5-10; John 12:20-33</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Will you pray with me?  May the
words of my mouth and the meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your sight
O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer. Amen!</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">So we have been walking in the
wilderness of Lent for over four weeks now, pondering, thinking, suffering,
hopefully learning while praying.</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Over the past few weeks in this
Lenten Wilderness, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">we have been considering perspectives.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We have considered how suffering
impacts our lives <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">and how to look above the mud-pit of
suffering. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We have looked at how to improve our
kindness and generosity. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We have wondered how we can be better
stewards of <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">God’s love and grace here on Earth.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">In all of this, you might have
noticed that we have prayed.</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"> <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We have read and heard Psalms. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We have offered invocations and confessions.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We have prayed and reflected.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">I would add some meditation, Tai Chi
and more. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">These are ways to lift joys, to
express concerns, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">to quiet our minds, to make space, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">and to be in the presence of God.</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Why do you pray? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Better, how do you pray?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">At the core, there are general
categories of prayer used to deepen expressions of humility, grace and love
through us.</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Is your prayer one of praise?  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">A little “praise Jesus” here and
there can be nice. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Some like to poke fun at more guttural
praising – diaphragm praises. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">There is something more here. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Moses brought down a set of
commandments with this at the top. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">At worship and many hymns, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">we celebrate and praise the glory of
God.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We are happy to praise God in good
times, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">celebration or new lives welcomed
into our family. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">(Isn’t it great to have this Church
that is welcoming and loving <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">all</i> of
God’s Children? )</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Of praising prayers, how about
sadness and suffering like funerals? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">That might feel awkward while singing
or praying powerful praise <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">during times of immense sorrow. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Perhaps, that is when we should be
praising God for the lives we have <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">and the souls that touch us. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">I enjoy the service as a “celebration
of life” where people celebrate this relationship.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">The question is raised of what are we
doing to honor that relationship now and going forward?<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>What are we doing to give praise to the lives
around us?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Then, we have prayers of
supplication. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We ask for protection, for intervention,
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">or for guidance for paths through
suffering. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">As an athlete, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">I have often asked for help in matches
and sparring with varied results.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">I would even bargain with God: <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">for a win, I would give up say
chocolate …for an hour? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">A biblical example is Jesus in the garden
before the infamous arrest <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">and on the cross.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">(Hebrew 5:5-10 reminds us of this.) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">That Jesus knows suffering, pain and
fear <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">might help us realize, again, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">that we are not alone in our
suffering and brokenness.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Jesus has been there and has walked a
few miles with us.</span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Then, there are prayers for
forgiveness. (I have done this many times.) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">This is <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">not</i> the “sorry-<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">you</i>-were-offended”
prayer. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">That might need a two-fer prayer.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Still, what good is asking for
forgiveness <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">when you are not willing to atone? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Instead, when we have strayed, when
we forget, or when we degrade someone, we did that to God.  Jesus
reminds us of this. (Matthew 25:31-46; Luke 9:46-48) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">In order to receive, we must first be
willing to give ourselves.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Are you willing to forgive others?
Are you willing to forgive yourself?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We don’t need to stay on strayed
paths, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">and I know that we can be our own worst
critic.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Thus, we might need to forgive
ourselves. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We can be humble because God is ready
to mother us any time. </span><span style="color: black; mso-ascii-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman"; mso-hansi-font-family: Calibri;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Finally, there are prayers of thanks.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">We are want to ask and ask and ask, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">but how many times do we stop and give
thanks?  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">How often do we give credit where
credit is due? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; font-size: 14.0pt;">Be thankful you woke up, for your
breath, for your family and friends <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">

 Walking with Prayerful Humility 
 
 Tony E Hansen 
 
 14 March 2018 
 

 
 
 A Vespers reflection based upon Psalm
51; Hebrews 5:5-10; John 12:20-33 
 

 
 
 Will you pray with me?  May the
words of my mouth and the meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your sight
O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer. Amen! 
 

 
 
 So we have been walking in the
wilderness of Lent for over four weeks now, pondering, thinking, suffering,
hopefully learning while praying. 
 

 
 
 Over the past few weeks in this
Lenten Wilderness, 
 
 we have been considering perspectives.   
 
 We have considered how suffering
impacts our lives 
 
 and how to look above the mud-pit of
suffering. 
 
 We have looked at how to improve our
kindness and generosity. 
 
 We have wondered how we can be better
stewards of 
 
 God’s love and grace here on Earth. 
 

 
 
 In all of this, you might have
noticed that we have prayed. 
 
 We have read and heard Psalms. 
 
 We have offered invocations and confessions.
 
 
 We have prayed and reflected. 
 
 I would add some meditation, Tai Chi
and more. 
 
 These are ways to lift joys, to
express concerns, 
 
 to quiet our minds, to make space, 
 
 and to be in the presence of God. 
 

 
 
 Why do you pray? 
 
 Better, how do you pray? 
 
 At the core, there are general
categories of prayer used to deepen expressions of humility, grace and love
through us. 
 

 
 
 Is your prayer one of praise?   
 
 A little “praise Jesus” here and
there can be nice. 
 
 Some like to poke fun at more guttural
praising – diaphragm praises. 
 

 
 
 There is something more here. 
 
 Moses brought down a set of
commandments with this at the top. 
 
 At worship and many hymns, 
 
 we celebrate and praise the glory of
God.   
 
 We are happy to praise God in good
times, 
 
 celebration or new lives welcomed
into our family. 
 
 (Isn’t it great to have this Church
that is welcoming and loving all of
God’s Children? ) 
 

 
 
 Of praising prayers, how about
sadness and suffering like funerals? 
 
 That might feel awkward while singing
or praying powerful praise 
 
 during times of immense sorrow. 
 
 Perhaps, that is when we should be
praising God for the lives we have 
 
 and the souls that touch us. 
 
 I enjoy the service as a “celebration
of life” where people celebrate this relationship.   
 
 The question is raised of what are we
doing to honor that relationship now and going forward?   What are we doing to give praise to the lives
around us? 
 

 
 
 Then, we have prayers of
supplication. 
 
 We ask for protection, for intervention,
 
 
 or for guidance for paths through
suffering. 
 
 As an athlete, 
 
 I have often asked for help in matches
and sparring with varied results.   
 
 I would even bargain with God: 
 
 for a win, I would give up say
chocolate …for an hour? 
 
 A biblical example is Jesus in the garden
before the infamous arrest 
 
 and on the cross. 
 
 (Hebrew 5:5-10 reminds us of this.) 
 

 
 
 That Jesus knows suffering, pain and
fear 
 
 might help us realize, again, 
 
 that we are not alone in our
suffering and brokenness.   
 
 Jesus has been there and has walked a
few miles with us. 
 
   
 
 Then, there are prayers for
forgiveness. (I have done this many times.) 
 
 This is not the “sorry- you -were-offended”
prayer. 
 
 That might need a two-fer prayer.   
 
 Still, what good is asking for
forgiveness 
 
 when you are not willing to atone? 
 
 Instead, when we have strayed, when
we forget, or when we degrade someone, we did that to God.  Jesus
reminds us of this. (Matthew 25:31-46; Luke 9:46-48) 
 
 In order to receive, we must first be
willing to give ourselves. 
 
 Are you willing to forgive others?
Are you willing to forgive yourself? 
 
 We don’t need to stay on strayed
paths, 
 
 and I know that we can be our own worst
critic. 
 
 Thus, we might need to forgive
ourselves. 
 
 We can be humble because God is ready
to mother us any time. 
 

 
 
 Finally, there are prayers of thanks.
 
 
 We are want to ask and ask and ask, 
 
 but how many times do we stop and give
thanks?   
 
 How often do we give credit where
credit is due? 
 
 Be thankful you woke up, for your
breath, for your family and friends 
 
 — the many gifts you have. 
 

 
 
 Be thankful that you were able to
play a good game. 
 
 Be thankful with humble heart and
your head up . 
 

 
 
 Despite our brokenness and suffering, 
 
 When you pray, remember 
 
 You are worthy of celebration; 
 
 You are worthy of guidance; 
 
 You are worthy of compassion; 
 
 because You are a child of God. 
 

 
 
 Whether you pray quietly or with
hands in the air, 
 
 I submit to you pray with your heart
and go ahead 
 
 — let the spirit move you.   
 
 Can I get an amen? 
 
 While you are praising, thanking, or
asking God, 
 
 if you listen carefully, you may
realize the presence all around you. 
 

 
 
 You can tap into that spirit anytime
and anywhere. 
 
   (No
matter where you are on life’s journey.) 
 

 
 
 Praise, supplication, contrition, and
thanksgiving are ways 
 
 that we can call to God 
 
 and ways that we can respond to God. 
 
 Are you willing to hear what God has
to offer? 
 
 How will you respond? 
 
 Are you doing anything that prevents
you from responding to God? 
 
 Are you ready to work with the gifts
that you have? 
 
 God is all around you nudging you and
listening. 
 
 Yet, are you listening? 
 

 
 
 As Children of God, 
 
 With prayer and humility, we can
witness God’s love, patience, kindness and generosity to us. 
 
 In these many ways, we pray to God
because we know that 
 

 
 
 God is good all the time 
 
 and all the time, God is Good 
 

 
 
 Let us share those prayers with God. 
 

 
 
 Thanks Be to God.

<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">A sermon based upon Psalm 118; </span><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">John
12:12-16<span style="color: black;"><o:p></o:p></span></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<a href="https://urbucc.org/2018/03/31/courage-to-go-forth/" target="_blank">(a link to the audio)</a><br />
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Will you pray with me?  Holy and gracious God,
open our hearts and minds to receive the lesson given to us today. May the
words of my mouth and the meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your sight
O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer. Amen!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">So we have been walking in the wilderness of Lent <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">And we are on the last leg with only a week left. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Perhaps this is one reason why we celebrate Palm Sunday.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">For another reason, our scripture this week focuses upon the
arrival of Jesus into Jerusalem.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The
Importance of This Story<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Each of the Gospels has a rendition of this arrival and that tells
us this is important. For the purposes of this discussion, I want you to
consider how courageous this was for Jesus. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let’s consider the context. People have been lifting mighty big
perceptions of Jesus all over countryside.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">People have heard and witnessed many things. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Many are starving for food and justice.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Many are starving for hope and what Jesus is saying.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The revolutionary sermons about the poor, equality, fairness and
real justice while challenging the stewards of power have made Jesus “famous.”<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The countryside is now full of whispers about Jesus.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let me remind you that, “A whisper in the ear can be
heard for miles.”<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We know how that “whispered” story will change over
time. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus unapologetically proclaims that which the people
have been starving to hear.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">For this, </span><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus has been called the Messiah. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">In their minds, Messiah is a great king, or general, <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">that has come “on a colt”<o:p></o:p></i></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">to save the people from oppression. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Yes, Jesus is not only preaching the Truth <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">that all people are deserving of God’s grace, love and
healing, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus calls out corruption and traditions that deform
God’s love for all people. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">It is necessary to note that the people outside of the
city are marginalized, and simply discarded for being sick or different. They
literally are the fringe of society. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The high priests have comfort with Jesus away in the
country, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The corrupt elites don’t want to care about the people
(or Jesus) outside those walls, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">but not this day.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;"><span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Speaking
Truth to Power<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today is the day the Lord has made for those whispers
to come to the city.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We know that Jesus has made many scribes uncomfortable,<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and Jesus means to bring that discomfort to Jerusalem.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus is taking this mission into the center of the aristocracy
that has profited from the corruption <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">by
the Pharisees and the Empire </i>-- The Lions’ Den. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">It is time to call out these people. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">It is time to face the music for their spiritual and emotional neglects.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus dares them “I am the face of the Truth” I am the body of the
oppressed.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus dares those that have tried to arrest and to kill him.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Perhaps Jesus could have lived longer and preached more had he
stayed out of Jerusalem<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">because those leaders heard Jesus criticizing them, and they
believe the Truth is a threat to their leadership. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">They want to silence Jesus, even like they did to John the
Baptist. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus also knows this. Yet our people cannot afford obliviousness
anymore.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today is the day the Truth cannot be quiet or hidden anymore. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today, Jesus brings the Truth to power because they are clearly not
taking hints. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today, the corrupt can no longer conveniently ignore the community
or the Truth. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today is the day to set things right. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">So what is the plan?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Instead of armed soldiers and trumpet fanfare, Jesus comes into
the city on a borrowed donkey with a rag-tag set of followers - No guns, no
weapons and no shields. A non-violent demonstration is a stark contrast to
Roman military, and thus, the Romans have little reason to consider Jesus a
threat. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Even with this, do you really think Jesus is without fear or
danger?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">With each step forward, Jesus can feel the burden getting heavier
and heavier as more and more people pray their hopes onto Jesus. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Each step is closer to another sword, and we have to wonder who is
hiding in the crowd.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The effort to step forward is borne by the donkey, and you have to
wonder if the donkey was also feeling the increasing weight. The courage to
keeping going forward rises with each step.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>The unknown, the potential of sabotage, assassination and more fear rise
as we get closer to the gate. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I can hear someone in the back asking, Tony that is powerful stuff
about Jesus, but what does that have to do with me?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I am glad you asked.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">If you were a follower of Jesus witnessing all the threats against
Jesus, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">would you have followed Jesus into this gate or would you have sat
back and waited?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Would you hold onto your fear of what <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">could</i> happen?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Would <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">you</i> have courage
to follow regardless of your own fears and discomfort?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Courage
Arises from Discomfort <o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">It is interesting to note that The word courage comes from the
Latin and French “Coeur.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">-- meaning the heart or in terms of courage “coming from the
heart.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Thus, to be courageous is to be whole-hearted.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We cannot be whole hearted while leaving parts of us behind<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Another perspective, Philosopher Alan Watts calls “fake courage” a
form of armor. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">This is to say that armor is used to hide both what is outside and
also what is inside our hearts. Therefore, real courage is possible through discerning
our suffering and our fears. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Real courage is understanding that our vulnerabilities are not
weaknesses. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Then, what is possible happens when we let our hearts be real and
authentic <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">-- by letting go of all that isn’t.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">It took me a long time to come to terms with who I was as a
person. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I kept my own armor to hide who I did not think I should be. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Even when the “secret” was out, I still kept hiding myself from
myself.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Even more, I let others define what I was and what I could be.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The delusion caused inner turmoil, mutilated my vulnerability, and
denied my authentic self. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I even questioned my own being. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">You know what God said to me?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">God said, I don’t want an illusion or a shell.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I want<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>you - authentic you.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Through miracle hands and voice of good people, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">God reached towards me and reminded me that I too was a Child of
God.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That God loved me and made me just the broken way I am.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">God says I too am worthy of love and dignity<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">So, God says let go of that armor.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">God says, Be bold and be who you are meant to be.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Letting go was not easy and came with its own discomfort. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">God says to connect and share your story<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and now here I am. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I am still learning, as we all are, but I learned also what<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Susan David says that “<a href="https://www.blogger.com/null" name="OLE_LINK2"></a><span style="mso-bookmark: OLE_LINK2;">discomfort is the price of admission to a
meaningful life.</span>”<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">You and I may want real justice and opportunity, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">but no matter how you spin it, discomfort is part of <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">feeling</i> our heart’s passion (aka
courage).<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We are all faced with our own mortality, our own discomfort. Steve Jobs said that when we live our lives realizing that death is going
to happen, we make no more excuses for things left undone. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Embrace your discomfort and embrace failure and fears – This is part
of authentic you.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Those qualities make you uniquely beautiful.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There are no guarantees in this life so you might as well make
your discomfort meaningful. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today is the day the Lord has made for you to have a meaningful
life. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">If we go living our life never taking the next step, we never move
from the spot we are. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">If we don’t get up from our comfortable bed, we never discover the
value of courage. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today is the day the Lord has made to wake up our heart’s passion,
our courage.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Waking up requires that we shed armor, take a chance and boldly be
who we are.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Susan David goes further, “courage is not an absence of fear;
courage is fear walking.” In other words, courage does not mean less fear. <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">I am sure that Jesus had some fear about the
many threats. </i>Courage means that despite our fears, we keep going, one step
at a time while revealing ourselves, our messiness, our hopes, our heart’s
passion and our courage. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Just like
the crowd on the steps of the Capitol. <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The courage to do right and to do justice is powerful.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There is a underlying theme in this story.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Courage is contagious. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Like Jesus, courage starts with one soul. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Courage then connects a community because we can’t do this alone.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">In fact, like whole-hearted courage cannot leave part of us
behind, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus, by being among the marginalized and fringes of society, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">shows us that we all are worthy of courage.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Courage of community invites all – no matter who you are, what
age you are, no matter where you are on life’s journey.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let me remind you, Jesus and the followers have no weapons.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The crowd notices this too <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">– Jesus is someone like us and walks proud without weapons.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">But wait, there’s more,<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">As more and more people join in,<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">the power of community is revealed: weapons or violence not necessary.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Maybe, they too were tired of violence and corruption like we are.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Maybe, they too were tired of being treated like social trash.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Maybe, the Spirit of God lifted hopes <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">And fed courage to be us – no weapons, no armies and no violence.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">To be honest, Jesus probably drew encouragement from the crowd.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We can draw upon the love, hope, kindness and exuberance of the
community.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Our community and children calls us to act<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">With their branches and blankets, people reveal their hopes in
Jesus’s mission. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">They give their solemn encouraging salute to keep going.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today is the day that With courage, we stand and walk together.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We encourage each other.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">(Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr made this pillars of their
work.)<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">What to Do
with Courage<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Perhaps it
is time time to exercise our hearts.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Can you
feel the hearts in this room rise? <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Can you
feel the motion and hope wanting to burst forth?<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">with all
of the energy and the Spirit around you!<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I am
almost surprised you are exercising while still seated <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">because
today is the day the Lord has made for you!<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">This day,
we remember how one can change.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">This day, we remember how one can inspire by daring to do what is
right.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I ask you
do you follow Jesus example?<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Do you
connect your heart to your community?<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The community needs you.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">God wants you!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today is the day<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">the right time is now.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There is no better time than right now to do the right thing.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">So, be an agent of change, and<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We start with ourselves.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I submit to you that what is in your heart is worthy of expressing.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today, you can speak truth to power. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today, you can speak truth to your family.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today, you can speak truth to friends<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When you are truthful to yourself.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Life is
hard and did not come with instructions. <span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> </span><o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus as
your example suggests<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">To go
boldly into what’s right<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Go boldly
into the lion’s den, tell your story.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">And people
will listen and will follow. <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is one reason why this trip into Jerusalem is so important.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Each of you deserve to be valued as worthy <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and through God, we have deserved grace.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We don’t want to be ignored or forgotten.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Through the community, we can share our story.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">This is the day the Lord has made for Jesus to ride <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">To be an example of one soul with courage <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That helped a community have courage.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let that example help us find our voice and our courage.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We may not choose what falls into our lap, but<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let’s go fear walking and let our courage and the Spirit guide us
into the light.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Be courageously authentic.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Embrace your discomfort.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Have the courage to speak the Truth.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When we open up and connect, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we open up to the power of love and community. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We can transform together. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Thus, Truly
tell yourself that you are worthy of love.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That you
are a Child of God.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Tell
yourself to have courage to be yourself.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Because my
hearing isn’t good…<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Turn to
the people next to you. <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Tell them
they are a Child of God.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Tell them
to have courage to be who they are.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Are you ready to fear walk with God in this wilderness?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Are you ready to have courage to go forth?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">This is the day the Lord has made, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let us courageously rejoice!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
